but behind the scenes, they wer
competitors.description:
Throughout 2025, PAW Chain’s public presence may have seemed quiet,

but behind the scenes, they were integrating with enterprise-grade custodians like Fireblocks and Coincover.

Why does this matter?

Because institutions can’t legally interact with blockchain infrastructure unless:
• Assets can be securely custodied
• Transactions follow policy controls
• Access is MPC-protected
• Recovery + insurance mechanisms exist

This is the compliance layer required before banks, funds, and asset managers are allowed to connect.

Not hype.
Infrastructure.

@PawChain is building toward institutional readiness.

competitors.title:
1. The Core Philosophy: "Bitcoin Stays Blind"

In standard bridges (like WBTC), there is a "Multisig
competitors.description:
1. The Core Philosophy: "Bitcoin Stays Blind"

In standard bridges (like WBTC), there is a "Multisig Wallet" on the Bitcoin network controlled by 5-10 entities (like BitGo). You have to trust them.

Alienc0der is saying: "Bitcoin should not verify the other chain (Zenon). Bitcoin must remain blind."
To the Bitcoin network, the transaction looks like a standard signature spend. Bitcoin does not say, "This transaction happened because tokens were burned on Zenon"; it simply says, "The signature is valid, transaction approved."

2. What is Witness Encryption?

This is the heart of the system.

Normally, to encrypt data, you need a Person (Public Key).

In Witness Encryption, you encrypt data to a Fact (NP Statement).

Example: I put Bitcoin in a box and program the lock as follows: "This lock will open if and only if a 'Burn Proof' (Witness) containing a specific transaction hash from the Zenon Network is presented."

The thing that opens the box is not a "Person" (Admin, Multisig member), but a Mathematical Proof.If that proof (Witness) exists, the encryption dissolves, and the Bitcoin is released. If the proof doesn't exist, all the computers in the universe combined cannot move that Bitcoin.

3. The Two Variants

Alienc0der mentions two different implementation methods here:

Variant A (Recommended - Signature Release):

Here, the "Private Key" is not encrypted.
Instead, the Signature of a pre-constructed Bitcoin transaction is encrypted.

Scenario: User burns zBTC on Zenon -> Generates Proof (Witness) -> Uses this proof to decrypt the package -> The package reveals only the signature required to execute that specific transaction.

Security: Even if the person decrypting it is malicious, the revealed signature only says "Send 1 BTC to User X." They cannot change it to "Send to User Y." At worst, they broadcast the transaction for everyone (which is what you want anyway).

Variant B (Obfuscated Contract):

A more complex method involving an "Obfuscated Smart Contract" (Smart Secret) that never reveals the key but outputs the signature. This is discussed more in Ethereum research circles (Suegami's research), but Variant A is cleaner and safer for Zenon.

4. The Implication for Zenon: "Programmability in Cryptography"

Alienc0der’s following sentence is critical:

"Programmability lives in cryptography, not Script"

Bitcoin's language (Script) is constrained ("No loops, no smart contracts"). Bitcoin L2s usually say, "Then let's change Bitcoin" (OP_CAT, covenants, etc.). Zenon says, "No, leave Bitcoin alone. We will embed the programmability into the Cryptography (Witness Encryption)."

In Summary: 
With this system, Zenon aims to become the first network to manage Bitcoin without the need for a Custodian. 
To convert Bitcoin to Zenon (zBTC), you don't trust a company; you trust mathematics (encrypted witness). If you burn zBTC on Zenon, the lock on the Bitcoin network opens automatically. There is no human in the middle, only the Witness.

https://t.co/rl8htxfXNZ

Crypto Needs 5,000 Banks — Not One Winner

Nathan McCauley of Anchorage Digital argues that the futu
competitors.description:
Crypto Needs 5,000 Banks — Not One Winner

Nathan McCauley of Anchorage Digital argues that the future of digital assets depends on plurality, not monopolies. Rather than one dominant player, crypto infrastructure must support thousands of banks, issuers, and institutions — each integrating stablecoins, custody, and tokenized assets in their own way. Anchorage’s role, he says, is to be infrastructure that enables that ecosystem to scale.

Speaking at Consensus Hong Kong 2026,
clients.description:
Binance CEO: Agentic AI Will Use Crypto as Its Payment Layer

Speaking at Consensus Hong Kong 2026, @Binance CEO @_RichardTeng said autonomous AI systems handling tasks like booking travel or making purchases will rely on crypto and stablecoins for seamless, cross border payments.

He pointed to blockchain’s speed and programmability as key advantages over traditional banking, enabling AI agents to transact instantly without human intervention.

The strong engagement around the remarks reflects growing investor focus on the AI crypto intersection and the potential emergence of a machine driven economy.

AgentCover Pro White Paper is now live.

Today, BDIC Insurance introduces a comprehensive crypto insurance framework built specifically for the emerging agentic AI payment economy.

As AI agents begin executing payments, micro-transactions, and cross-border settlements autonomously, new categories of risk are emerging. Traditional insurance products were not designed for this shift.

Built on BDIC’s decentralized insurance architecture, including our dual-tier risk framework and 33% reserve structure  , AgentCover Pro extends our mission of protecting digital assets into the next phase of blockchain adoption.

This is not speculation. It is infrastructure for programmable finance.
